title: Governance, Risk and Compliance
summary: Assess risk, map controls across NIST CSF 2.0, ISO/IEC 27001 and CIS Controls, prepare audit evidence and assess suppliers, through five practical labs.
description: A practical programme in security governance, risk assessment, control frameworks, audit readiness and third-party risk, including Nigerian data protection obligations under the NDPA 2023. You will build a risk register, map controls to CSF 2.0, review an ISMS scope and Statement of Applicability, test controls against evidence, assess a hosting supplier, and learn to report risk to executives. All labs use fictional organisations and synthetic data. ISO standards are explained in AMANIQ's own words and are not reproduced.
audience: Aspiring GRC analysts and security auditors
Compliance and risk professionals moving into cybersecurity
IT managers responsible for security policy
prerequisites: Professional working experience in any field
outcomes: Build and maintain a risk register
Use NIST CSF 2.0 profiles for gap analysis
Explain ISMS concepts and certification accurately
Assess third-party and data protection risk
inclusions: Digital badge and verifiable certificate on completion
Access to course version 1 for the period set out in the terms

faqs.q: Is this an ISO/IEC 27001 auditor qualification?
faqs.a: No. AMANIQ certificates confirm course completion only. ISO auditor qualifications are awarded by accredited certification and personnel bodies.

faqs.q: Do I need to buy the ISO standards?
faqs.a: No. Lessons explain the concepts in our own words. If your organisation implements an ISMS, it should purchase the official standards from ISO or a national standards body.

faqs.q: Is the data protection content legal advice?
faqs.a: No. It is educational. Consult qualified legal counsel and the NDPC's current guidance for compliance decisions.

faqs.q: What do I need to pass?
faqs.a: Complete all required lessons, pass all five labs, and score at least 75% (30 of 40) on the final examination.

labs.title: Build a risk register from a business scenario
labs.summary: Rate likelihood and impact for five risks at a fictional microfinance company and choose an appropriate treatment for each.

objectives: Rate likelihood and impact against defined criteria
Choose treatments consistent with risk appetite
content.scenario: **Ọja Microfinance Ltd** (fictional) has 40 staff, a core banking application hosted by a supplier, and a mobile app used by 30,000 customers. The board's risk appetite statement says: *any risk rated 15 or above (likelihood × impact) must be treated; risks rated 4 or below may be accepted.*
content.scope: Use only the scenario documents. Ratings use 1 (very low) to 5 (very high).
content.instructions: Read the context documents, then complete the register. Each row is checked against an acceptable range agreed by AMANIQ assessors; you need at least 75% of entries within range.
content.simulationNotice: This is a simulation. All data is synthetic and generated by AMANIQ Academy for training. No real systems, people or organisations are involved, and nothing you do here leaves the platform.

documents.title: Likelihood and impact criteria
documents.body:
| Rating | Likelihood | Impact |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 5 | Expected within a year | Regulatory sanction, loss of licence, or > ₦100m loss |
| 4 | Likely within a year | Major customer harm or ₦20m–₦100m loss |
| 3 | Possible within a year | Noticeable disruption or ₦5m–₦20m loss |
| 2 | Unlikely | Minor disruption |
| 1 | Rare | Negligible |

documents.title: Context interview notes
documents.body:
- Staff share the core banking admin password; MFA is not enabled. Phishing emails targeting staff arrive weekly.
- Customer data backups are taken nightly but have never been test-restored.
- The office generator is serviced quarterly; power cuts are frequent but brief.
- The mobile app's supplier holds ISO/IEC 27001 certification and contractual liability insurance for breaches.
- A legacy fax machine stores no data and is used once a month.

hints: Shared admin passwords plus weekly phishing make compromise likely, with severe impact.
The fax machine risk is trivial on both axes.

rows.label: R1 Unauthorised access to core banking via shared admin credentials
R2 Inability to restore customer data after ransomware
R4 Breach at mobile app supplier

feedback.correct: Your register is consistent with the criteria and the board's appetite.
feedback.incorrect: Re-read the criteria table and the appetite statement; at least 75% of entries must fall within the assessed range.

documents.title: CSF 2.0 Functions (summary)
documents.body:
- **Govern**: strategy, expectations, policy, roles and oversight.
- **Identify**: understanding assets, risks and improvement needs.
- **Protect**: safeguards to manage risk.
- **Detect**: finding and analysing possible attacks and compromises.
- **Respond**: actions regarding a detected incident.
- **Recover**: restoring assets and operations after an incident.

tasks.prompt: Map each control to its primary CSF 2.0 Function.
hints: Asset inventories help you understand what you have.
Board-approved policy is about direction and oversight.

rows.label: Incident response playbook and on-call rota

feedback.incorrect: Revisit the Function definitions; at least six of eight must match.

content.scenario: **Ìrìn Payroll Services Ltd** (fictional, `irinpayroll.example`) runs payroll for 140 corporate clients on its own platform, *PayFlow*. Its first ISO/IEC 27001 Stage 1 audit is in six weeks. The CEO has asked you, as an internal reviewer, to check the scope statement and a sample of the Statement of Applicability (SoA) before the auditors see them.
content.scope: Use only the documents provided. SoA rows describe controls in Ìrìn's own words; they are not quotations from the standard.
content.instructions: Read the scope statements, risk register extract and interview notes, then review each SoA row. For the grid, choose the single most important issue with each row (or 'Acceptable'). You need at least 7 of 9 rows right.

documents.title: Organisation profile
documents.body:
- 85 staff across the **Ikeja operations office** (payroll operations, client support, finance) and the **Yaba engineering office** (12 developers who build and maintain PayFlow).
- PayFlow is hosted in a colocation facility in Lagos operated by a supplier, *Ebute DataHalls Ltd* (fictional). Ìrìn owns and administers the servers; the supplier provides power, cooling and physical security.
- Since 2025, operations and engineering staff work from home two days a week on company laptops.
- Ìrìn's website states: *"Our payroll services are ISO/IEC 27001 certified"* (planned for after the audit).
- No software development is outsourced.

labs.title: Collect and assess evidence for selected controls
labs.summary: Test joiner and leaver access controls by sampling system records, judge the quality of backup evidence, and reach audit conclusions.

objectives: Test operating effectiveness by comparing records from independent systems
Judge evidence for reliability, timeliness and sufficiency
Reach and express a supportable control conclusion
content.scenario:
You are on **Ọja Microfinance Ltd**'s internal audit team (fictional). The audit covers **1 July to 31 December 2025** and three controls:

- **AC-02** Every new joiner's access to core banking is approved by their line manager *before* the account is provisioned.
- **AC-05** Leavers' accounts are disabled no later than the next business day after their last working day.
- **BK-01** A restore of core banking data is tested at least once per quarter and the result recorded.
content.scope: Use only the datasets and documents provided. All joiners and leavers in the period are included in the HR extracts, which come from the HR system and are treated as complete.
content.instructions: Compare the HR population with the IT records, review the backup evidence submitted by IT, then answer the tasks. Business days are Monday to Friday; there were no public holidays in the relevant weeks.

| EV2 | Screenshot of the backup console banner reading "Last restore test: Successful". No date or system clock is visible. |
| EV3 | Restore test record from the backup system dated **14 Jun 2025**, job log attached. |
| EV4 | Email from the IT manager to internal audit: "We test restores every quarter and they always work." |
| EV5 | Backup Standard v2, approved March 2025, section 4: "Restores must be tested at least quarterly." |
| EV6 | Restore test record from the backup system: core banking database restored on **9 Dec 2025**, integrity check passed; job log attached; signed off by the IT manager and the head of operations. |

tasks.prompt: How many joiners had a ticket whose account was **provisioned before** the approval was recorded?
hints: Compare ApprovedAt with ProvisionedAt in AccessRequests, row by row.

tasks.prompt: Which joiner (EmployeeId) has an active core banking account but **no access request at all**?
hints: Every joiner in HRJoiners should appear in AccessRequests. Which one is missing?

tasks.prompt: Select **all** leavers whose accounts were **not** disabled by the next business day after their last working day.
hints: Look up each HRLeavers row in CoreBankingAccounts.
A last day on Friday means the account must be disabled by the following Monday.

tasks.prompt: For BK-01, decide whether each item submitted by IT is acceptable evidence that a restore test operated during the audit period, and give the main issue.
hints: The audit period is 1 July to 31 December 2025.
Evidence of the requirement is not evidence that the control operated.

tasks.prompt: What is the most appropriate conclusion for **AC-02** over the audit period?
hints: How many of the 12 joiners were provisioned without prior approval, including the one with no ticket?

options.label: Effective: the control operated throughout the period
Effective with a minor, isolated exception
Not operating effectively: 3 of 12 joiners received access without prior approval
Cannot conclude: HR data cannot be used as a population

tasks.prompt: In the AC-02 finding, which statement is the **criteria** element?
hints: Criteria describe what was required, not what was found.

options.label: Three of 12 joiners in the period received core banking access before approval or without any request
Access must be approved by the line manager before the account is provisioned (control AC-02)
Staff may hold unauthorised access to customer accounts, increasing fraud risk
Enforce approval in the ticket workflow before provisioning is possible

feedback.correct: Correct: SD-4820 (E1007) and SD-5034 (E1011) were provisioned before approval.
feedback.incorrect: Compare ApprovedAt with ProvisionedAt for each ticket.

feedback.correct: Correct: E1009 has an account created on their start date but no request or approval.
feedback.incorrect: Match every HRJoiners EmployeeId against AccessRequests.

feedback.correct: Correct: E0942 was disabled a week after the deadline and E0958 is still active.
feedback.incorrect: Check DisabledAt against each last working day; remember weekends.

feedback.correct: Good judgement: only EV1 and EV6 are reliable, dated records from within the period.
feedback.incorrect: Check each item's date, source and whether it shows the control operating. At least 9 of 12 entries must match.

feedback.correct: Correct: a quarter of joiners bypassed approval, which is not an isolated exception.
feedback.incorrect: Count the exceptions: two early provisions and one joiner with no ticket.
Criteria state the requirement the condition is measured against.

labs.title: Assess a third-party hosting provider
labs.summary: Tier a fictional hosting supplier, analyse its questionnaire, certificate, assurance report and draft contract, and make a recommendation.

objectives: Tier a supplier and choose proportionate due diligence
Identify red flags across self-reported and independent evidence
Assess contract clauses against your own obligations
Make and justify a risk-based recommendation
content.scenario: **Ọja Microfinance Ltd** (fictional) plans to move its new loan origination platform to **Àpótí Cloud Hosting Ltd** (fictional, `apoti-cloud.example`). The platform will store personal data for about 30,000 customers, including identity numbers, salary details and bank statements. Downtime would stop all new lending. The head of lending wants to sign next month and has asked the GRC team for a due diligence opinion.
content.scope: Use only the documents provided. This is an educational exercise and not legal advice.
content.instructions: Review the documents, then answer the tasks. Note that self-reported answers and independent evidence sometimes disagree.
content.simulationNotice: This is a simulation. All data is synthetic and generated by AMANIQ Academy for training. No real systems, people or organisations are involved, and nothing you do here leaves the platform.

documents.title: Ọja supplier tiering criteria
documents.body:
| Tier | Criteria (any one is sufficient) |
| --- | --- |
| Critical | Stores or processes customer personal or financial data at scale (> 1,000 customers) **or** its failure would stop a critical service |
| High | Processes staff personal data, or has network access to Ọja systems |
| Medium | Holds limited contact data; no system access |
| Low | No data and no access |

**Ọja obligations relevant to suppliers**
- Ọja must notify the NDPC within 72 hours of becoming aware of a qualifying personal data breach. Ọja policy requires processors to notify Ọja within **24 hours**.
- Ọja policy: customer personal data may leave Nigeria only with DPO approval and a documented transfer basis.
- Ọja policy: high-severity penetration test findings at critical suppliers must be fixed within 90 days.

documents.title: Àpótí security questionnaire (self-reported, February 2026)
documents.body:
| # | Question | Àpótí response |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 1 | Is MFA enforced for all administrative access? | Yes, hardware keys for all platform administrators. |
| 2 | Is customer data encrypted at rest? | Yes, all storage volumes encrypted with AES-256; keys in a hardware security module. |
| 3 | Backups? | Daily, replicated to our second data centre in Lagos; restore tested quarterly. |
| 4 | Do you use sub-processors for customer data? | **No.** |
| 5 | Penetration testing? | Annual external test; last test June 2025 found 2 high-severity issues. One fixed; one "remediation in progress". |
| 6 | Breach notification to customers? | Within **30 days** of confirming a breach. |
| 7 | Where is customer data stored? | Ikeja data centre (primary) and Lekki data centre (backup). |

documents.title: Certificate and assurance report summary
documents.body:
**ISO/IEC 27001:2022 certificate** issued by an accredited certification body; valid to May 2027.

> *Scope:* "Provision of colocation and data centre facility services at the Lekki data centre."

**Independent assurance report** (service organisation controls, operating effectiveness, 1 Apr 2025 – 31 Mar 2026), managed hosting service:

- Auditor's opinion: controls were suitably designed and operated effectively, **except** that in 3 of 25 sampled staff departures, administrator access was removed more than 5 days after the leaving date.
- Subservice organisations: *"Database administration support is provided by Northgate DBA Services (fictional), operating from outside Nigeria, which has remote access to customer database servers."*
- Complementary user entity controls: *"Customers are responsible for managing their own application user accounts, including enforcing MFA for their users and reviewing their users' access."*

documents.title: Draft contract: security and data protection schedule
documents.body:
| Clause | Text (summary) |
| --- | --- |
| CL1 | Àpótí will process Customer personal data only on Customer's documented instructions and will keep it confidential. |
| CL2 | Àpótí will notify Customer of a personal data breach within 30 days of confirming it. |
| CL3 | Àpótí may engage sub-processors at its discretion. |
| CL4 | Customer may audit Àpótí once a year on 30 days' notice, or may instead rely on Àpótí's current independent assurance report. |
| CL5 | On termination, Àpótí will return Customer data in a standard format on request and delete it within 30 days, providing written certification of deletion. |
| CL6 | Àpótí's total liability for data breaches is limited to one month's fees. |

tasks.prompt: Which tier should Àpótí be assigned?
hints: Apply Ọja's tiering criteria to the scenario.

tasks.prompt: Select **all** findings that are significant concerns requiring action before contract signature.
hints: Compare the questionnaire with the independent evidence.
Compare the supplier's commitments with Ọja's own obligations and policy.

options.label: The ISO/IEC 27001 certificate covers only the Lekki colocation facility, not the managed hosting service in Ikeja
A database support provider outside Nigeria has remote access to customer databases, though the questionnaire says there are no sub-processors
A high-severity penetration test finding from June 2025 is still open
Storage volumes are encrypted with AES-256
Hardware keys are used for administrator MFA
Backups are replicated to a second Lagos data centre

hints: Does each clause support Ọja's obligations and policies in the tiering document?

rows.label: CL4 Annual audit right or assurance report
CL5 Data return and certified deletion
CL6 Liability capped at one month's fees

tasks.prompt: Under data protection law, what is Àpótí's role in relation to Ọja's customer data?
hints: Who decides why and how the data is processed?

tasks.prompt: According to the assurance report, which control must **Ọja** operate itself for the assurance to hold?
hints: Read the complementary user entity controls.

options.label: Physical access control at Àpótí's data centres
Managing and reviewing its own application users, including MFA

tasks.prompt: What should the GRC team recommend to the head of lending?
hints: The business owner decides; GRC gives a risk-based opinion with options.

options.label: Approve as proposed: the supplier is ISO certified

Approve only with conditions: revise CL2, CL3 and CL6; disclose and assess the sub-processor and obtain DPO approval for the transfer; obtain assurance covering the Ikeja hosting service; agree a dated fix for the open high finding; record residual risk with the business owner
Reject: any supplier with an open finding must be refused
Defer indefinitely until the supplier has no findings at all

feedback.correct: Correct: customer financial data at scale and a critical service.
feedback.incorrect: Apply the Critical criteria to 30,000 customers' data and a lending outage.

feedback.correct: Correct: four concerns, two of which contradict the self-reported questionnaire.
feedback.incorrect: Look for gaps between the questionnaire and independent evidence, and between the supplier's terms and Ọja's obligations.

feedback.correct: Correct: notification, sub-processor and liability terms do not support Ọja's obligations.
feedback.incorrect: Compare each clause with Ọja's 24-hour notification policy, its transfer rule and the size of the potential loss. At least 5 of 6 must match.

feedback.correct: Correct: Àpótí processes data on Ọja's behalf; Ọja remains the controller and accountable.
feedback.incorrect: Ọja decides the purpose and means of processing.

feedback.correct: Correct: the report assumes customers manage their own application users.
feedback.incorrect: Read the complementary user entity controls in the assurance report summary.

feedback.correct: Correct: a proportionate, conditional approval with a recorded residual risk.
feedback.incorrect: Look for the option that addresses each concern without assuming certification answers everything.

questions.prompt: Which activity is primarily a governance responsibility?

options.text: Setting the organisation's appetite for information security risk
Rating the likelihood of a phishing scenario

questions.explanation: Governance sets direction, appetite and accountability; the other activities support risk management and compliance.

questions.prompt: "How to enrol a new staff member's phone in the authenticator app" belongs in which document type?
questions.explanation: Step-by-step instructions are procedures.

questions.prompt: Who should normally own the risk of fraud through a lending application?

options.text: The business leader responsible for lending

questions.explanation: Business leaders own the risks their activities create; security advises and internal audit provides assurance.

questions.prompt: In a 12-person company one administrator must both grant and remove system access. Which is the best compensating control?

options.text: Ask the administrator to be careful
A monthly independent review of access changes by a manager outside IT
Remove all logging to protect privacy
Document that segregation is impossible and take no action

questions.explanation: Where full segregation is impossible, an independent review compensates.

questions.prompt: Which TWO are key risk indicators?

options.text: Number of critical vulnerabilities older than 30 days on internet-facing systems
Number of privileged accounts without MFA

questions.explanation: KRIs signal rising exposure; output counts do not.

questions.prompt: A customer contract requires notification of security incidents within 24 hours. Where should this be recorded?

options.text: In the obligations register, with an owner and evidence of compliance
Nowhere; contractual terms are not compliance obligations

questions.explanation: Contracts are a source of obligations and need owners and evidence.

questions.prompt: "Backups have never been test-restored" is best described as a:
questions.explanation: It is a weakness that a threat such as ransomware could exploit.

questions.prompt: Why should a 5×5 risk score of 20 not be described as "twice as risky" as a score of 10?

options.text: Because the scale is ordinal: the numbers rank risks but do not measure them proportionally
Because likelihood and impact must be added, not multiplied
Because scores must be expressed in naira

questions.explanation: Qualitative matrices rank risks; arithmetic on them is limited.

questions.prompt: A risk is rated 20 before controls and 8 after MFA is enforced. What is 8?

options.text: The target risk, regardless of evidence

questions.explanation: Residual risk is the rating after current controls, valid only if the controls are proven to work.

questions.prompt: A company retires an unsupported system rather than securing it. Which treatment is this?
questions.explanation: Stopping the activity avoids the risk.

questions.prompt: The board's tolerance is that no customer-data risk may stay above 9 for more than 90 days. A risk rated 16 has had no treatment plan for five months. What should happen?

options.text: Lower the rating to 9 so it fits the tolerance
Escalate to the authority named in the governance framework for a treatment decision or formal acceptance

questions.explanation: Breaches of tolerance must be escalated; ratings should never be adjusted to fit appetite.

questions.prompt: Which TWO elements are missing from the risk statement "Ransomware"?

options.text: The vulnerability that would be exploited
The asset affected and the business impact
The name of the ransomware group's leader
The colour used on the heat map

questions.explanation: A rateable scenario links threat, vulnerability, asset and impact.

questions.prompt: Which list contains the six NIST CSF 2.0 Functions?

options.text: Govern, Identify, Protect, Detect, Respond, Recover
Plan, Do, Check, Act, Review, Improve
Identify, Protect, Detect, Respond, Recover, Report
Prevent, Detect, Correct, Deter, Recover, Comply

questions.explanation: CSF 2.0 added Govern to the five Functions of version 1.1.

questions.prompt: Establishing roles, responsibilities and authorities for cybersecurity risk management falls under which CSF 2.0 Function?
questions.explanation: GV.RR (Roles, Responsibilities, and Authorities) is a Govern Category.

questions.prompt: What is the main purpose of comparing a Current Profile with a Target Profile?

options.text: To identify gaps that form the basis of a prioritised action plan
To rank the organisation against competitors

questions.explanation: The gap between profiles drives the improvement plan.

questions.prompt: Which statement about CSF Tiers is accurate?

options.text: Every organisation should aim for Tier 4
Tiers are the same as CSF Functions
Tiers characterise the rigour of risk governance and management practices and should be chosen to suit the organisation's risk
Tiers are awarded by NIST after an audit

questions.explanation: Tiers describe practice rigour; they are not a mandatory maturity target or a certification.

questions.prompt: Where would you find illustrative actions showing how an organisation might achieve a specific CSF 2.0 Subcategory?

options.text: In the Implementation Examples published by NIST

questions.explanation: NIST publishes Implementation Examples and Informative References online alongside the Core.

questions.prompt: A small accounting firm with no software developers is building its first Target Profile. What is the best approach?

options.text: Set the highest rating for every Subcategory
Copy a large bank's Target Profile
Set targets based on its own risks, obligations and appetite, accepting lower targets where outcomes matter less
Leave Govern out because the firm is small

questions.explanation: Targets come from the organisation's own risk context.

questions.prompt: Which statement about ISO/IEC 27001 certification is correct?

options.text: Accredited certification bodies certify organisations after an external audit
Completing a training course makes a person ISO 27001 certified

questions.explanation: Certification bodies certify; accreditation bodies accredit them; certificates have a limited life with surveillance audits.

questions.prompt: Which SoA entry is most likely to be raised as a finding?

options.text: Outsourced development excluded because no development is outsourced
Remote working controls excluded because "all staff work on site", while staff work from home two days a week
Backup control included to treat a data-loss risk, with dated restore records
Policy control included with a recent approval date

questions.explanation: Exclusions must be credible for the actual scope.

questions.objective: Explain the role of Annex A
questions.prompt: How should Annex A be used in a risk-based ISMS?

options.text: Implement all 93 controls regardless of risk
Select controls to treat assessed risks, then compare with Annex A to check nothing necessary was overlooked
Ignore it, since it is optional guidance only
Use it instead of a risk assessment

questions.explanation: Controls follow from risk treatment; Annex A is a completeness cross-check.

questions.prompt: Why is ISMS scope important to customers reading a certificate?

options.text: It shows the price of the certification
It shows which services, locations and activities the certification actually covers
It replaces the need for a risk assessment

questions.explanation: A certificate covers only its stated scope.

questions.prompt: What normally happens in years two and three of an ISO/IEC 27001 certification cycle?

options.text: Surveillance audits covering parts of the ISMS
A new Stage 1 audit each year

questions.explanation: Certification bodies perform periodic surveillance audits between certification and recertification.

questions.prompt: An internal audit finds that two leavers kept access for a month because HR emails to IT were missed. Which is a corrective action rather than a correction?

options.text: Triggering account disablement automatically from the HR system's leaver record

questions.explanation: Corrective action removes the cause; correction fixes the instance.

questions.prompt: Which TWO are typical outputs of an ISMS management review?

options.text: Decisions on resources and changes to the ISMS

questions.explanation: Management review produces leadership decisions, not certificates.

questions.prompt: A small organisation with limited IT staff is starting with the CIS Controls. Where should it begin?
questions.explanation: IG1 is essential cyber hygiene and the recommended starting point.

questions.prompt: Why do inventories of enterprise and software assets come first in the CIS Controls?

options.text: You cannot secure, monitor or patch assets you do not know you have
Auditors only test the first two Controls
They replace the need for access control

questions.explanation: Visibility underpins every other control.

questions.prompt: A CIS Safeguard and a CSF Subcategory overlap but the CSF outcome also covers identity proofing. How should the mapping be described?

options.text: Partial (the Safeguard is a subset of the outcome)

questions.explanation: State the relationship; most mappings are partial.

questions.prompt: Which is a corrective control?

options.text: Restoring systems from tested backups after ransomware

questions.explanation: Corrective controls limit damage and restore operations.

questions.prompt: What is the difference between a control owner and a control operator?

options.text: The owner is accountable that the control exists and works; the operator performs it
The operator approves the control; the owner performs it

questions.explanation: Separating accountability from performance supports segregation of duties.

questions.prompt: A legacy application cannot support MFA. Which is the strongest compensating control?

options.text: Access only through a jump server that enforces MFA, with session recording reviewed weekly, approved as a time-limited exception

questions.explanation: A compensating control should address the same risk to a similar degree and be formally approved and reviewed.

questions.prompt: Which policy statement is best written?

options.text: Appropriate security should be applied where possible
Remote access to company systems must require multi-factor authentication
Use the VPN product currently installed
Staff are encouraged to think about security

questions.explanation: It is mandatory, technology-neutral and testable.

questions.prompt: Which policy exception record is complete?

options.text: Requirement not met, reason, resulting risk, compensating controls, approver at the right level, expiry date and remediation plan
A verbal agreement with the CISO

questions.explanation: Exceptions need risk, compensating controls, authorised approval and an expiry.

questions.prompt: Why keep previous versions of a security policy after it is updated?

options.text: To show what the policy required at a given time, for example during an investigation or dispute
Because policies may never be deleted by law in every country
So staff can choose which version to follow

questions.explanation: Archived versions support investigations, audits and disputes.

questions.prompt: In a traceability matrix, a technical control exists that no policy or standard requires. What does this suggest?

options.text: Work that nobody mandated, which may be unfunded, inconsistent or unknown to governance
The control should be deleted immediately

questions.explanation: Controls without policy backing are a traceability gap in the other direction.

questions.prompt: When is it cheapest to address security requirements for a new system?
questions.explanation: Requirements defined early avoid costly redesign.

questions.prompt: Which TWO are typical inputs to a security architecture review?

options.text: Applicable security standards, such as logging and encryption

questions.explanation: Designs are reviewed against principles, patterns and standards.

questions.prompt: Which evidence is most reliable for showing an access review took place last quarter?

options.text: A system-generated review record showing reviewer, date and decisions

questions.explanation: Reliable, dated, system-generated records are strongest.

questions.prompt: A quarterly access review is performed faithfully but covers only email accounts, while the key risk is core banking access. This is a:
questions.explanation: The control, even when performed, does not address the risk.

questions.prompt: To test whether all joiners received approved access, which population should you sample from?

options.text: Access tickets in the service desk queue
The list of joiners from the HR system
Accounts the IT manager remembers creating

questions.explanation: The population must not depend on the control being tested.

questions.prompt: Independently recomputing which leavers still have active accounts is an example of:
questions.explanation: Re-performance repeats the control independently and is the strongest technique.

questions.prompt: Which element of an audit finding explains *why* the condition occurred?
questions.explanation: Cause leads to an effective corrective action.

questions.prompt: The same access-review finding has appeared in three consecutive annual audits. What does this most strongly indicate?

options.text: Corrective actions are not addressing the root cause, which is a governance issue to report to the board
The control should be removed from scope

questions.explanation: Repeat findings show that corrective action is ineffective.

questions.prompt: Which supplier most needs the deepest due diligence?

options.text: A hosting provider storing all customer financial records
A marketing agency with no data access

questions.explanation: Tier by data sensitivity, access and criticality.

questions.prompt: When reading a supplier's independent assurance report, what are complementary user entity controls?

options.text: Controls the supplier expects its customers to operate for the assurance to hold

questions.explanation: Customers must operate these themselves.

questions.prompt: A supplier's questionnaire says it uses no sub-processors, but its assurance report names an offshore database support company with remote access. What should you do?

options.text: Trust the questionnaire, since the supplier wrote it
Treat the contradiction as a red flag; require disclosure and assessment of the sub-processor and check transfer requirements
Ignore it if the supplier is ISO certified

questions.explanation: Independent evidence that contradicts self-reported answers needs follow-up.

questions.prompt: Which TWO clauses most directly support a clean exit from a supplier?

options.text: Return of data in a usable format
Certified deletion of data within a defined period

questions.explanation: Exit clauses cover data return and deletion.

questions.prompt: Due diligence on a critical supplier finds a weak notification clause and an open high-severity finding, but otherwise strong controls. What is the most appropriate recommendation?

options.text: Approve with conditions: contract changes, a dated remediation plan, and residual risk recorded with the business owner
Ask the supplier to self-certify that the issues are fixed

questions.explanation: Proportionate, conditional approval with recorded residual risk is usually best.

questions.prompt: Who decides the purposes and means of processing personal data?
questions.explanation: Controllers decide why and how; processors act on their instructions.

questions.prompt: Under the Nigeria Data Protection Act 2023, within what period must a controller notify the Commission of a personal data breach likely to result in risk to individuals' rights?

options.text: Only at the next annual filing

questions.explanation: The Act requires notification to the NDPC within 72 hours of becoming aware of such a breach.

questions.prompt: A loan app collects customers' entire phone contact lists "in case they are useful later". Which principle is most clearly breached?
questions.explanation: Collect only what is needed for specified purposes.

questions.prompt: When should a data protection impact assessment be carried out?

options.text: Before processing that is likely to result in high risk to individuals
Only when the regulator requests one
Every five years for all processing

questions.explanation: DPIAs assess and reduce risk before high-risk processing starts.

questions.prompt: A processor suffers a breach of a controller's customer data. Which statement is correct?

options.text: The controller remains accountable and must have chosen and contracted the processor appropriately
Nobody is accountable because the breach was external
The data subjects are accountable for sharing their data

questions.explanation: Controllers remain accountable for personal data they entrust to processors.

questions.prompt: What should open an executive risk report?

options.text: A description of the assessment method
The headline conclusion and any decision required
A list of all control identifiers

questions.explanation: Lead with the conclusion; detail goes in appendices.

questions.prompt: Which is the best way to describe a risk to a board?

options.text: "A likely compromise of core banking could expose 30,000 customers' data and trigger regulatory sanction; ₦18m over six months brings it within appetite"

questions.explanation: Boards decide on impact, cost and options, with honest likelihood.

questions.prompt: Which remediation action should usually come first?

options.text: A large, expensive project that closes many low-rated gaps
A low-cost action that substantially reduces a risk above appetite, such as enabling already-licensed MFA

questions.explanation: Prioritise by risk reduction per unit of effort.

questions.prompt: Why should a GRC analyst avoid overstating risks to win budget?

options.text: Credibility is lost when exaggerated risks do not materialise, weakening future reports
It shortens the report too much

questions.explanation: Honest uncertainty preserves trust in future reports.
